[RFCS.23.5] **`asserted_at`, and no `event_id`.** A `FactExternal` carries
no `event_id`: an `event_id` identifies a fact only within the engine that
stamped it ([LFST.5.6]). A fact that must be recognised on another tier
carries an identifier of the author's in one of its slots ([LFST.7.2.4]).
`asserted_at` is the instant the fact entered working memory, as the engine
clock read it: a UTC instant, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, the value
`now()` would have given at that moment. A fact a rule publishes enters no working
memory on its way out ([LTIE.4.3]), so its `asserted_at` is the instant of the
`publish`. If the wall clock had no value at that
moment ([LTIM.2.8.3]), `asserted_at` is absent: `has_asserted_at` is false, and
the fact leaves the engine without an instant. It reproduces on replay, because the engine clock is a recorded
input, and migration keeps it. It describes the fact, not the write: a fact
stored later carries the time it was asserted.
